I mucked around, and tested similar setups in 4.4 and 3.6.1. The results are very similar. 

Somewhat surprisingly (or not, idk a lot about integrated graphics architectures) the Mobile renderer seems to be the fastest on my particular hardware, at around 5ms for reading a single value from a mipmapped screen texture.

This is just an expensive operation. That's why we made mipmaps optional in Godot 4.0. It is especially expensive on fill-rate bound hardware like mobile phones and iGPUs. 

The cost comes from doing a full Viewport copy. Basically the normal rendering process needs to stop, then copy over every single pixel then resume. It's even worse with mipmaps. 

The cost also strongly correlates with your screen resolution. So if you are running with anything more than 1080p you will really feel the performance impact.

As a rule, you should be doing full screen copies sparingly. In general you should rely on the BackBufferCopy node with a limited rect size so you are only doing a partial screen copy.

> The cost comes from doing a full Viewport copy. Basically the normal rendering process needs to stop, then copy over every single pixel then resume. It's even worse with mipmaps.

I'm wondering if a post-processing API would be able to decrease the cost compared to needing to sample `screen_texture`. In fact, right now, I wonder if a compositor effect can have a lower cost for a post-processing effect that only needs the color buffer.
Ya, doing a proper post processing API would reduce the cost in this case. As would using a Viewport instead of using the screen texture.

I tried rendering to a viewport and then displaying it's texture through the shader. I hope this is what you meant by using a viewport. This seems to work to speed up the resample to 2.5ms, the problem is now I lack mipmaps on the texture, which I was going to use to cheapen the blur effect 😅. Hopefully additional texture samples won't cost as much now, I'll try to see if I can get an acceptable performance level by sampling the blur myself, and report my findings.

I'm trying to see if Calinou's suggestion would work. Compositor effects seem kind of expensive on 2D games, since they seem to require a whole 3D pipleine setup: I've also tried to combine the two optimizations, but I can't seem to be able to grab a viewport texture in a compositor effect. ~The RID returned by the rendering server for the viewport texture doesn't seem to correspond to a texture on the GPU according to the rendering device. Do you know if this is possible at all? All I can find is just examples of creating textures on the rendering device, or grabbing the whole screen buffer instead of a specific viewport buffer/texture.~ Found some help on how to do this correctly here: https://github.com/pink-arcana/godot-distance-field-outlines/discussions/1#discussioncomment-14352648 Sadly it doesn't come with any performance improvements over just using the compositor normally. (Also, sorry for spamming an issue with this stuff, maybe this is better suited for a help forum. But I feel like the iGPU I have is probably representative of the machines most 2D games will be targeting, so figuring out how to get good performance out of them could be useful for other people. I can move it to conversations if you wish.)

I was going insane trying to understand why do I suddenly have huge performance dips without any processing in scripts at all. I even updated my graphics drivers. But it appears that `BackBufferCopy` periodically does *something* that completely tanks performance. The "Distortion" and "Glow" nodes have screen reading shaders (with `filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic`) on them. If I remove `BackBufferCopy` node the performance is going to dip once (for some unknown reason). But if I put `BackBufferCopy` between these node, every couple (2-5) of seconds the performance dips from 2.5ms to 20ms. Sadly Godot's visual profiler lacks any relevant info so it's not possible to infer what exactly is getting done inside the "Render CanvasItems" section when the dips happen. This is how it looks.
> Apologies This is not a problem on 4.2. Should I create a new issue or is there one already?
